questions.prompt: What is Chapter 3 mainly claiming about attention?
choices: Attention only helps people remember information later
Attention helps determine what feels important, not just what gets noticed
Attention always leads people to the truth faster

explanation.gentle: The chapter says attention changes felt importance, not only awareness.
explanation.direct: Option B captures the central mechanism. Attention is evaluative as well as perceptual.
explanation.competitive: The spotlight does not just reveal. It ranks.

questions.prompt: Why can the same feature feel more decisive after it is foregrounded?
choices: Because foregrounding changes its perceived weight in judgment
Because foregrounding changes the underlying facts automatically
Because people stop thinking once something is highlighted

explanation.gentle: The feature itself may be unchanged. What changes is how much weight the mind gives it.
explanation.direct: Option A is right. The chapter is about shifted significance, not altered reality.

questions.prompt: Which distinction does Chapter 3 insist on keeping visible?
choices: The difference between deserved importance and attended importance
The difference between memory and imagination
The difference between hearing and seeing

explanation.gentle: The chapter keeps warning that what feels important is not always what deserves the most weight.
explanation.direct: Option A is the crucial limit. Spotlighted significance and earned significance can overlap, but they are not the same thing.

questions.prompt: Iris can lead with one product feature before a client decision. What is the strongest Chapter 3 move?
choices: Lead with the feature that genuinely deserves the most weight in a good judgment
Lead with the flashiest feature, because flash always deserves rank
Avoid any sequence at all so the client feels completely neutral

explanation.gentle: The chapter allows spotlighting, but it insists that the spotlight should match real priority.
explanation.direct: Option A fits the mechanism and the limit. Foregrounding is powerful, so it should be used in service of proper rank.
explanation.competitive: If Iris spends the spotlight on glitter, she teaches the client the wrong hierarchy.

questions.prompt: What is the main trap when a room keeps returning to one vivid detail?
choices: The detail becomes automatically false
The room may start treating the most attended detail as the most important one by default
The room will stop remembering everything else forever

explanation.gentle: The chapter warns that attention can quietly promote one feature into the top rank whether it earned that rank or not.
explanation.direct: Option B is the trap. Salience can become significance without a proper audit of the whole field.
explanation.competitive: The bright object starts billing itself as the whole case.

questions.prompt: Ben's class presentation kept circling one highlighted chart while stronger context faded. What does Chapter 3 say likely happened?
choices: The chart became the most attended feature and therefore gained too much weight
The chart changed the underlying evidence more than the other slides
The class decided charts are always more truthful than words

explanation.gentle: The chart likely took over because it owned the foreground, not because it necessarily deserved the top rank.
explanation.direct: Option A matches the chapter's mechanism. Foregrounding altered the room's weighting system.
explanation.competitive: Ben's slide won the spotlight and then stole the verdict.

questions.prompt: Kara notices that one repeated family concern starts feeling like the whole decision. What is the best explanation?
choices: Repetition and attention gave that concern extra psychological rank
Repeating a concern automatically makes it objectively more serious
Family conversations cannot weigh more than one issue at a time

explanation.gentle: The concern may still be real, but the chapter says repetition can also increase felt importance beyond what it deserves.
explanation.direct: Option A is right. The mechanism is weighting through attention, not truth creation.
explanation.competitive: The repeated issue got heavier because it stayed onstage.

questions.prompt: Why might Milo's whiteboard choice change the whole meeting before anyone argues the merits?
choices: Because large visual emphasis can convert salience into perceived importance quickly
Because whiteboards make people less rational than screens do
Because the first written item is always the true cause of the problem

explanation.gentle: The chapter says display choices can act like weighting choices. What is big and focal can start feeling central.
explanation.direct: Option A fits the mechanism exactly. The board is helping assign rank before full evaluation.
explanation.competitive: The marker is deciding gravity before the meeting thinks it is deciding gravity.

questions.prompt: When does the use of attentional spotlighting become hardest to defend?
choices: When it helps a neglected but real priority receive proper weight
When it inflates a vivid but secondary feature into the main issue
When it is used in any persuasive setting at all

explanation.gentle: The chapter's warning is about manufacturing significance, not about attention itself.
explanation.direct: Option B captures the ethical limit. Spotlighting becomes harder to defend when it assigns weight a feature has not earned.
explanation.competitive: The move goes bad when the spotlight rigs the hierarchy instead of revealing it.

questions.prompt: If a foregrounded feature already feels most important, what is the most natural next step for the book to examine?
choices: Why the same foregrounded feature may also start feeling causal
Why importance has nothing to do with explanation
Why only expert persuaders can use attention strategically

explanation.gentle: The bridge is natural: once the spotlighted feature feels weighty, it is close to feeling explanatory too.
explanation.direct: Option A is the next logical escalation. Importance is the runway for causal credit.
explanation.competitive: First the spotlight wins rank. Next it wants blame or credit.
